profile.name: Merci Ruyanga
profile.title: Backend Engineer
profile.headline: I build backend systems that institutions run on every day.
profile.summary: Backend-focused full-stack engineer with 4+ years of experience designing, building, and deploying production web applications. I specialize in scalable backend architecture, microservices, event-driven systems with Apache Kafka, and REST and GraphQL APIs, using Python (Django, FastAPI), Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, and Redis. I work across the full lifecycle, from system design and secure authentication to cloud deployment on AWS.
profile.about: I am a final-year Computer Science student at the University of Rwanda, and most of what I know I learned by shipping. Several systems I built are used daily by university staff, students, and innovators across multiple campuses. I like problems where the hard part is understanding how people actually work, then turning that into software that is reliable, secure, and easy to maintain.

profile.projects_intro: Systems built for real users. Each one covers the problem and how I solved it.

profile.contact_intro: Hiring for a backend or full-stack role, or have a system that needs building? I usually reply within two working days.

projects.title: INUMA
projects.tagline: Staff travel approvals for the University of Rwanda, across every campus.
projects.description: A request-flow management system that digitized the local mission (staff travel) process, replacing slow paper approvals.
projects.problem: Every travel request has to pass several approvers in a set order, and the chain changes with the staff member's role and campus. Every action must be recorded, and no request can be lost or approved out of order.
projects.approach: I mapped the real approval process first, then modeled approval steps as data in PostgreSQL so chains are configurable rather than hard-coded. NestJS services move each request to the next approver automatically. Role-based access control with JWT restricts every action, and audit trails log who did what and when. Mission orders are issued with a verifiable QR code.

projects.title: UR Graduation System

projects.title: Agribridge
projects.tagline: A digital marketplace connecting Rwandan farmers, sellers and buyers, with payments protected until delivery.
projects.description: Agribridge lets farmers list produce and buyers source in bulk without intermediaries. When an order is larger than one farmer can supply, nearby listings are pooled into a single sale, and farmers can also group up to buy seed and fertiliser at better prices. Buyers pay by mobile money or bank transfer; the money is held until both sides confirm delivery, and every completed sale builds the seller's reliability score. Available in Kinyarwanda, English and French, and installable as an app that works offline.

labs.title: Resilient Delivery-Photo Platform with Cross-Region Recovery
labs.summary: Production-style platform that stores proof-of-delivery photos for a logistics client. Photos live in a private, versioned S3 bucket replicated to a second region, order details in Multi-AZ PostgreSQL, and the app runs on ECS Fargate behind CloudFront and AWS WAF, released blue/green through CodePipeline.
highlights: Cross-Region Replication to a Glacier Instant Retrieval bucket, with bucket policies that block permanent deletes
Multi-AZ RDS PostgreSQL with rotating Secrets Manager credentials, 7-day point-in-time restore and AWS Backup copies to a second region
CloudFront as the only public entry point: Origin Access Control for media, WAF rejects requests that bypass the CDN
Blue/green releases with CodeDeploy, alarm-based rollback and one-click redeploy of any of the last 10 versions

labs.title: Zero-Downtime Container Platform on ECS Fargate
labs.summary: Containerised order service running in private subnets with no internet route, released blue/green from GitHub to ECS. Five CloudFormation stacks separate network, delivery foundation, service and release pipeline, all deployed by Git sync.
highlights: GitHub Actions pushes images to ECR with short-lived OIDC credentials: no AWS access keys anywhere
CodePipeline with a manual approval gate, then CodeDeploy blue/green with automatic rollback on 5xx alarms
Tasks reach AWS only through VPC endpoints; no NAT gateway, no public IPs
Target-tracking auto scaling from 2 to 6 tasks, verified under load and during a simulated AZ failure

labs.title: Auto-Scaling Order System for Peak Sales Days
labs.summary: EC2-based order system built to survive sales-day traffic: servers across two Availability Zones behind a load balancer, scaling on CPU, and bootstrapped entirely from user data with no SSH. One CloudFormation template, deployed by Git sync, with a costed estimate of USD 129 a month.
highlights: Auto Scaling group with CPU target tracking and rolling replacement that keeps a server in service during releases
Servers install and start the app at boot from a pinned Git tag, then signal CloudFormation when healthy
No key pairs or port 22: administration through Session Manager, IMDSv2 required
Scripted demos for load testing, server failure and full Availability Zone failure

labs.title: Secure Multi-AZ Network for an Order System
labs.summary: Highly available, private-by-default VPC for an order system. Customers reach the front end through a load balancer spanning two Availability Zones, internal services have no inbound path from the internet, and engineers manage every server without open ports or keys.
highlights: Six subnets across two AZs (public, web, internal) with a NAT gateway per AZ and a free S3 gateway endpoint
Chained security groups: internet to ALB, ALB to web tier, web tier to internal services only
VPC Flow Logs, a monthly AWS Budgets alert and a written cost analysis
Every requirement traced to the template line that meets it

labs.title: Keyless Container Delivery to Amazon ECR
labs.summary: CI/CD for a Django REST API: every pull request is linted, tested and smoke-tested in Docker, and every merge to main publishes an image to Amazon ECR using GitHub OIDC instead of stored credentials.
highlights: GitHub Actions assumes an IAM role through OIDC, limited to the main branch
Images tagged with the commit SHA and pushed only once per commit
ECR lifecycle policy keeps the 20 most recent images and expires untagged layers
CodeBuild buildspecs for running the same build and tests inside AWS

labs.title: GitOps Identity & Access Onboarding
labs.summary: Repeatable, auditable onboarding of engineers into an AWS account, managed entirely as code. Every access change goes through Git, is deployed by CloudFormation Git sync, capped by permission boundaries and recorded by CloudTrail.
highlights: Least privilege by ceiling: permission boundaries hold even if a broader policy is attached later
Permissions granted to groups through AWS managed policies only, with no inline policies
First-login passwords generated by Secrets Manager, never stored in Git
Multi-region CloudTrail to an encrypted, versioned bucket with log file validation
